nodes.title: TAGGED REF2VA — ACTIVATES @TAGS PER SCENE
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the man in @hero_face, late 20s to early 30s, olive complexion, wavy dark brown collar-length hair, trimmed beard and mustache, black leather motorcycle jacket open over a burgundy maroon crew-neck tee, charcoal slim jeans, and black sneakers with white soles.
@hero_face is the multi-angle character reference sheet defining <Subject 1> facial identity, hair, beard line, and bone structure.
@storyboard is the 4x4 labeled scene board reference for shot composition across panels A1-D4; panel A1 anchors this segment.
summary:
[reference generation] Segment 1/12 (6s): cinematic horror short-film beat — farmhouse exterior approach. <Subject 1> identity locked from @hero_face; composition guided by @storyboard panel(s) A1. Photorealistic IMAX-scale dread, cold desaturated grade, no dialogue unless noted.
retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - exact face, hair, beard, leather jacket, burgundy tee, and jeans from @hero_face across every visible frame.
@storyboard (A1): fully_preserved - camera angle, subject placement, lighting intent, and story beat follow the referenced board panel(s) for this segment.
detailed_description:
The target video uses a cinematic horror film grammar: shallow depth of field, motivated practical light, heavy negative space, and subtle handheld micro-drift. Color is cold blue-green with crushed shadows and selective warm accents only where lamps or moonlight justify it.
[Shot 1] The segment opens on the storyboard composition for panel A1: farmhouse exterior approach. <Subject 1> occupies the frame with exact identity from @hero_face — jaw line, stubble, wavy hair, open leather jacket and maroon tee visible whenever framing allows. Environment textures read photoreal: peeling paint, dust in light beams, wet floor reflections where applicable.
[Shot 2] At 00:02.000, the camera pushes or pans with restrained horror pacing, maintaining spatial continuity from @storyboard panel A1. Sound design favors low room tone, distant creaks, and the subject's controlled breathing; no music unless scene demands a sting.
The segment holds tension for 6.0 seconds total, ending on a micro-cliffhanger suitable for seamless continuation into the next timed segment.
overall_soundscape:
Low-frequency room rumble, distant house settling, faint fluorescent buzz, soft footfall texture on wood or tile, no crowd noise.
non_diegetic_music:
None — horror tension carried by diegetic ambience and silence breaks only.

nodes.title: HOW TO WORK WITH V2
widgets_values:
1. Open the Scene Prompt Editor and select a scene. It edits the connected Plan directly.

2. Click @ Reference. The tray shows only references active for that scene and their current native labels. Hover an image/video tag to preview it. Hover audio for controls; it never autoplays. Click a chip to insert its stable @tag.

3. Queue from scene 1, or set Loop Start's range/resume controls. The Scheduled Ref2VA node compiles stable tags to native H3 labels and inserts no prompt text.

4. Review Gate pauses after each saved scene. Approve to continue, edit+retry to replace only that scene prompt, reroll for a new seed, or approve+stop to keep a recoverable partial.

5. Final Assemble uses %date:yyyy-MM-dd%. Existing exports are never overwritten: later runs receive _001, _002, and so on. The amber recovery branch remains muted until you need assembly without rerendering.
